_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `Puzzle5dMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.puzzle.5d` assembly document and its twenty-eight typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-puzzle-5d-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` (the seven members — note `kindCompatibility` is TOP-LEVEL here where both siblings file it inside `meta`), rules 1, 2, 4 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the twenty-eight committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets — which are the only statement of four things: that a grip list is INSIDE the part, so removing a grip CASCADES into the fasteners addressed to it; that deleting a part severs every fastener naming any of its grips; that `replace-part2d-geometry` rebuilds shape and extent from four arguments, dropping every member whose argument is null, while leaving the facet's placement and text alone; and that `replace-kind-catalogs` with a NULL argument is a NO-OP rather than a removal. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `puzzle-5d-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-fem2d-1`, `mutate-fem3d-1` and `mutate-gismap-1`, which took Python second implementations over this same carrier. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: STEP AP214, glTF, USD and IFC all carry an element placed in ONE space, none of them carries a part placed in a diagram and in a model simultaneously with a joint addressed as `"<partId>:<gripId>"`, and none of them reads this carrier. ALL TWENTY-EIGHT KINDS ARE ADJUDICATED AND NONE IS REFUSED, and this subset settles a question both siblings leave open: `mutate-puzzle-2d-1` and `mutate-puzzle-3d-1` each commit exactly one `replace-<container>-<port>` vector and each declares it `mutation.no-op` with an unchanged after-snapshot, while the corresponding `replace-part-grip` vector HERE really does rekind `grip-1`, on a grip a fastener is attached to, and the document moves — evidence that the verb is implemented and that being attached does not block it, which narrows the three readings those two siblings report. Its `null-catalogs-is-noop` vector likewise settles that the null argument is accepted and does nothing, which is what makes the siblings' missing catalogue inverse a gap in the VOCABULARY rather than in an implementation. A FINDING THE REFERENCE MADE WHILE BEING WRITTEN: this subset's `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️.json`, like both siblings', is not a mutation schema at all — it declares the SNAPSHOT's members, the pre-migration whole-snapshot-shaped generic schema that `s.architect.program`'s own mutation schema records itself as superseding — so the verbs and their argument lists had to be read off the committed payloads instead. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES: the SUBJECT half does not run this subset's codec — `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-puzzle-5d-1/🦀️.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today it establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, not yet our codec against a second producer. A `puzzle5d_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum closes it; it is not added here for two reasons, and neither is that the verb is hard: it is PRODUCTION code in a crate this test-side pass deliberately does not touch, and it could not be verified end to end today anyway. `parity` was not measured for any case in this pass: the single-case probe `parity exhaustive --owner 🗒️note --case mutate-note-1` was killed at the runner's OWN 900 s per-case budget while still COMPILING the generated subject host — the runner's message names the cause, shared cargo target-dir lock contention from a concurrent session — and then threw `spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT` out of `runProbe` with no summary line at all. `📓️w14-final-audit.md` §5.3 measured the underlying blocker one day earlier (`unresolved import component::component_persistent_local` in `semio-framework-plugin`, which sits in every generated host's dependency graph); this pass did NOT re-verify whether that is still the state, and says so rather than repeating it as fact. This subset's own plugin crate compiles clean at `cargo check --lib`. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 140 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `puzzle-5d-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 28-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.
